title: Shared Memory/Database Message Bus
pattern: Using a relational database or shared disk files as a high-frequency polling queue to communicate between services.
why_bad: It triggers high database contention and disk I/O. Polling queries lock tables constantly, inflating CPU utilization and causing lock escalation.
detection: An infinite polling loop in application code constantly querying a single table for state changes.
counterexample: Using specialized distributed message queues (like RabbitMQ or Kafka) or database Change Data Capture logs.
fix: Migrate communication to an event-driven system using standard messaging middleware.
